root_cause.text: The `bq257xx_reg_dt_parse_gpio()` function returns early when failing to retrieve a subchild node without first releasing the reference to the parent `child` device node via `of_node_put()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `of_node_put(child)` was moved to execute before the `if (!subchild)` check, ensuring the reference to `child` is released even when `subchild` is NULL and the function returns early.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a device node reference leak by releasing the parent node before the early return check.
intent_record.what: Moved the of_node_put(child) call to occur immediately after of_get_child_by_name, before the null check on subchild.
intent_record.how: Ensures that the reference count on the 'child' device node is properly decremented even if of_get_child_by_name fails and the function returns early, preventing a reference leak.

commit 981dd162b63578aee34b5c68795e246734b76d70
Author: Chris Morgan <macromorgan@hotmail.com>
Date:   Thu Sep 4 11:05:29 2025 -0500

    regulator: bq257xx: Add bq257xx boost regulator driver
    
    Add support for the boost regulator found in the Texas Instruments
    BQ25703. The boost regulator is capable of outputting between 4.48
    and 20.8 volts and between 0 and 6.35 amps.
    
    Signed-off-by: Chris Morgan <macromorgan@hotmail.com>
    Reviewed-by: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
bic_trace_step.reason: In the function `bq257xx_reg_dt_parse_gpio()`, the `child` node is retrieved using `of_get_child_by_name()`, which increments its reference count. When attempting to retrieve `subchild` on line 114, if `subchild` is NULL, the function returns early on line 116 without calling `of_node_put(child)`. This causes a reference count leak of the `child` node.
